minor.issue: Side-effect: retest_provider() unconditionally writes ANY test result (including transient PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE from a Pixabay network hiccup) into media_provider_status.status. A single upstream flake demotes a proven-working provider to DEVELOPER_SETUP_REQUIRED and BLOCKS all subsequent searches until re-tested. Observed live during this iteration — pixabay_video flipped from CONNECTED → PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE mid-run despite the stored key being valid. Search-dependent tests in this iteration had to _ensure_pixabay_active() (retry test) as a workaround. Recommend: on transient failures (PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE / RATE_LIMITED), keep the last-known status and only append a 'last_test_code' field, or require N consecutive failures before demoting.

action_items: OPTIONAL — Harden POST /api/media-library/providers/{id}/test so a single transient PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE does not demote a working provider. See minor issue above. This is not a spec violation (the current behaviour is 'honest current state') but it makes the /test button footgun-prone in the UI — one click on a bad-network moment blocks Pixabay search + produce-proof until someone clicks Test again.

OPTIONAL — Pixabay API rejects per_page < 3 with 400. If the UI ever exposes per_page it should clamp to 3..30. Currently /search hardcodes per_page=12 default and produce-proof uses 5, so no user-facing bug — surfaced only from adversarial tests.
critical_code_review_comments: media_library.retest_provider() overwrites status with any code returned by test_connection(). Recommend: only overwrite on CONNECTED / INVALID_KEY / PERMISSION_DENIED; treat PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE and RATE_LIMITED as transient and keep last-known good status (see minor issue).

media_library.test_connection() returns 'INVALID_KEY' for HTTP 400. Pixabay returns 400 for legitimately invalid params (e.g. per_page=1), not only for a bad key. If someone ever calls test_connection() with a valid key but a query that triggers 400, the key gets branded INVALID_KEY. Consider distinguishing 400 from 401 more strictly and requiring the response body to indicate an auth failure before mapping to INVALID_KEY.

media_production._tts() catches all exceptions and returns a string on failure. Good honest fallback. However, the returned string is placed into the step 'detail' via f-string, which will leak internal error text (potentially including a partial API key path or file system paths) to any authenticated super_admin caller — acceptable given super_admin only, but consider sanitising.
media_production._srt() computes cue count via NARRATION.count('.') and there's a stray space in the f-string 'NARRATION.count('.') ' at line 162 producing awkward output. Trivial.

produce_showcase() writes into MEDIA_ROOT = /app/backend/rendered_assets/media_masters and never cleans up job dirs. Currently 4 dirs on disk. Consider a retention policy (keep last 5 or the assets referenced by media_assets, prune the rest) — otherwise disk grows every proof run.

routers/media_library.py::produce_proof runs synchronously in the HTTP request thread; a 60s ffmpeg render blocks the request. If a client times out the client-side but the render finishes, media_assets + factory_milestones get updated anyway (idempotency via {code: 'QRU-MILESTONE-001'} upsert saves us). Consider making produce-proof background-job + progress-poll for MO-021 v2.

MediaLibrary.js runProof() has no client-side timeout config; if the backend takes >30s (default axios timeout in api.js if any), the UI could show a false 'Production pipeline failed' toast while the pipeline still completes. Confirm api.js timeout is at least 180000ms for this call, or route it through a separate axios instance.

MediaLibrary.js does not surface the credential audit log (GET /providers/{id}/logs) anywhere in the UI. Backend supports it; consider a small 'History' expander per provider card so super_admins can see validate/save/test/revoke events.

MediaLibrary.js registerAsset() posts collection='QRU General Backgrounds' hardcoded regardless of the result's actual kind or theme — audio results will register under a video collection. Consider deriving from the search context or prompting the user.

rca of the issue: One transient observed: POST /api/media-library/providers/pixabay_video/test occasionally returns test_code=PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE when the outbound HTTP call to Pixabay experiences a network hiccup. Because retest_provider() unconditionally $sets media_provider_status.status = <that code>, the provider is demoted from CONNECTED → PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, which makes provider_status() report status='DEVELOPER_SETUP_REQUIRED' (line 155: active := status=='CONNECTED') and blocks POST /search and POST /produce-proof with 'Pixabay Video is not activated'. Reproduction: hammer POST /providers/pixabay_video/test in a loop for ~30s; eventually one call returns PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE and the next GET /providers shows DEVELOPER_SETUP_REQUIRED even though the stored key is still valid — evidenced by another /test call within 2s returning CONNECTED. Mitigation deployed in test file: _ensure_pixabay_active() re-tests up to 5 times with 2s spacing before any search-dependent test. Recommended code fix (in media_library.retest_provider): only $set status when code in ('CONNECTED','INVALID_KEY','PERMISSION_DENIED'); on PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE / RATE_LIMITED, only update last_validated + emit a credential log event, do NOT overwrite the last-known-good status.
